A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eddy viscosity concept, which was developed for the study of turbulent boundary layers, can be used successfully in the case of turbulent jets and plumes as well.

, for every case studied, a solution was found which was characterized by the following properties: (1) mathematical similarity, (2) dynamic similarity, (3) similarity of the eddy diffusivity, (4) similarity of the mean velocity, (5) similarity of the temperature (or salinity), and (6) similarity of the turbulent kinetic energy.
we have found the analytical solutions for the mean flow and temperature (or salinity), for all the cases of jets and plumes with and without crosswind and with and without entrainment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in order to solve problems involving turbulent jets and plumes, one should use the power-law solution and, in addition, the appropriate form of eddy viscosity.

, in order to obtain the correct analytical solution of a turbulent jet or plume, one must first find the correct form of the ed dy viscosity, which depends on the particular problem under consideration.
